taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists the species as Pond Slider; the red-eared slider is one subspecies (T. s. elegans) of Trachemys scripta.
fieldMarks: Bright red horizontal streak behind each eye
Shell 10-29 cm, greenish-yellow to gray, brown or black, rough and indented; plastron usually yellow with dark spots
behavior: Primarily diurnal; basks on sunny days and is gregarious
Generally inactive in winter in the north
habitat: Quiet water with abundant aquatic vegetation, soft bottom and basking sites; tolerant of pollution.
range: Native from Michigan to Argentina, east of New Mexico. Established outside its range in many areas including Florida, New York and New Mexico; Animal Diversity Web also lists Canada.

lookalikes.name: Painted turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Two yellow patches behind each eye instead of the slider's single red streak (per Animal Diversity Web).
